svg.title: Data loads: from chunk to inference
svg.desc: Five stages left to right: chunk by consumer (CPU, GPU, proximity), encode at the edge (binary, Base64, UTF-8 vs ASCII), load dynamically (Base64 SWF then, WASM now), orchestrate in YAML (Kubernetes, placement, front matter), infer by reader (humans, agents, machines).

g.text: Data loads: from chunk to inference
GPU / CPU / proximity chunking → Base64 and UTF-8 at the edge → dynamic load → Kubernetes YAML → inference for people, agents and machines
SVG: CDATA holds JS, CSS, JSON
Get a URI and a hash,
THE HOTEL VERSION · CHUNKS TRAVEL LIKE GUESTS: PACKED TO FIT, TAGGED, KEYED, CHECKED AT EVERY DOOR, CHECKED OUT CLEANLY
Memory safe = no key outlives its permission.
Like DRM for data access: the key expires, is bound to one reader, is checked at every door and can be revoked. Hand out keys, not copies.
Binary holds the data. UTF-8 and Base64 are adapters at text-only boundaries.
Chunk to the consumer's natural unit, encode only at the edge, and describe every chunk in front matter so agents read the description and machines fetch the bytes.
ASCII ⊂ UTF-8: every ASCII byte is valid UTF-8, and the Base64 alphabet (A–Z a–z 0–9 + / =) is ASCII, so Base64 passes through any UTF-8 channel unchanged.
